study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Single-site recruitment at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University; no named public dataset.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "A total of 100 first-episode, untreated patients diagnosed with OCD were recruited from outpatient services within the Department of Psychiatry at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University... Healthy controls (HCs, n = 106) were enlisted from the community"

answer.SINGLE-SITE: HCs used to train normative model; OCD patients used for deviation maps and subtyping

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Gaussian process regression trained on HCs (age/sex) and applied to each patient.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs... This trained model was then applied to each patient"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Wen2025.pdf.md: Methods / Subtyping analysis based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities

model-1.model-name: gray matter volume normative model (Gaussian process regression)
